# Florence 1490 – Scientific method & philosophical ideas

- **Scientific method (conjecture, test, publish, repeat)** [`scientific_method`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_method.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Workshop trials, astronomical observations and medical case histories give investigators local precedents. A repeatable test of a stated explanation is easier to show than to institutionalise. Local: botteghe (workshop trial and error); Leonardo da Vinci (Milan).
- **Test claims instead of trusting authority** [`empiricism_over_authority`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/empiricism_over_authority.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept low. Poliziano compares manuscripts, while Benivieni investigates causes of death in bodies. Both offer precedents for checking a received account against evidence. Local: Antonio Benivieni (autopsies); Angelo Poliziano.
- **Controlled comparison (experiment with control group)** [`controlled_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/controlled_trial.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Avicenna's Canon lays out conditions for testing a drug's effects. Santa Maria Nuova offers a setting for comparing outcomes in similar patients. Local: Santa Maria Nuova hospital (many comparable patients).
- **Placebo effect and blinded trials** [`placebo_blinding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/placebo_blinding.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. That belief helps healing is accepted (imagination, faith, relics); deceiving a patient for a test offends physicians.
- **Correlation, causation and confounding** [`correlation_causation_confounding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/correlation_causation_confounding.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Scholastic logic names the fallacy post hoc; astrology and miasma medicine ignore it daily.
- **Selection and survivorship bias, fair sampling** [`selection_bias_sampling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selection_bias_sampling.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Humanists know Cicero's story of Diagoras and the votive tablets. Churches such as Santissima Annunziata are full of ex-votos. Local: Santissima Annunziata (wax votive figures).
- **Measurement and quantification** [`measurement_quantification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/measurement_quantification.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Balances already guide assayers and merchants. Cusanus's De staticis experimentis (1450) proposes extending weighing to medicine and natural philosophy. Local: abacus masters; assayers of the Zecca (mint).
- **Nature follows simple mathematical laws** [`mathematical_laws_of_nature`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mathematical_laws_of_nature.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Accepted for music, optics, perspective and the heavens; Platonists like the idea. Earthly motion is held to be qualitative (Aristotle). Local: Marsilio Ficino; painters' perspective (Alberti, Piero della Francesca).
- **Falsifiability (risky, testable predictions)** [`falsifiability`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falsifiability.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. A physician's prognosis or an astrologer's forecast can be checked against events. Agreeing in advance what observation would refute a claim is a further step.
- **Fallibilism (all knowledge of nature is provisional)** [`fallibilism_provisional_knowledge`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fallibilism_provisional_knowledge.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Academic scepticism is known from Cicero; Sextus Empiricus exists in Greek manuscripts in Florence. Doubt about doctrine is dangerous. Local: San Marco library; Medici library (Greek manuscripts).
- **Weighing evidence (base rates and Bayesian updating)** [`bayesian_reasoning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bayesian_reasoning.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Bankers and underwriters revise estimates when news of wars, pirates or defaults arrives. Numerical probabilities and a general updating rule would be new.
- **Reproducibility and open publication** [`reproducibility_open_publication`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reproducibility_open_publication.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Craftsmen protect valuable recipes, but printed technical books and circulating manuscripts already share some procedures. Independent repetition could give a workshop claim wider credibility.
- **Systematic errors of human judgement (cognitive biases)** [`cognitive_biases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cognitive_biases.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium
- **Formal logic (valid deduction and fallacies)** [`formal_logic`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/formal_logic.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Aristotelian syllogistic and fallacies are taught at every university (Peter of Spain). Humanists mock it as hair-splitting. No symbolic logic. Local: Studio of Pisa and Florence; Dominicans of San Marco and Santa Maria Novella.
- **Parsimony (Occam's razor)** [`occams_razor`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/occams_razor.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Known to scholastics as a rule of the nominalists. Platonists multiply spirits, spheres and hidden virtues freely.
- **Thought experiment** [`thought_experiment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/thought_experiment.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Scholastics argue 'secundum imaginationem' (Buridan, Oresme); the conclusions count as exercises, not as findings about nature.
- **Source criticism (testing documents and reports)** [`source_criticism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/source_criticism.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Valla challenged the Donation of Constantine in 1440. Poliziano's Miscellanea (1489) compares variant readings. Both give humanists examples of testing a text's authority. Local: Angelo Poliziano; Medici and San Marco libraries.
- **Consent and ethics of experiments on people** [`informed_consent_research_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/informed_consent_research_ethics.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Hospitals and courts hold power over patients and prisoners. A requirement for voluntary, informed participation in research would need explicit institutional backing.
- **Natural causes (naturalism about disease, weather, comets)** [`natural_causes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_causes.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Aristotle's Meteorology gives natural causes for comets, quakes and lightning, yet all are also read as signs. Plague is God's punishment plus bad air. Local: Girolamo Savonarola (prophecy of the scourge); Lucretius readers.
- **Scepticism towards astrology, omens, witchcraft and transmutation** [`scepticism_superstition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scepticism_superstition.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Astrology is court science (Ficino). Pico writes his attack on it in 1493–94. Malleus Maleficarum appeared 1486; alchemists seek patrons. Local: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola; Marsilio Ficino.
- **Atomism (matter is made of tiny particles in motion)** [`atomism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomism.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Lucretius (found 1417, printed 1473) is read as poetry; atoms mean Epicurus, mortal souls and impiety. Ficino burned his own early commentary. Local: Lucretius manuscripts in Florence; Michele Marullo (poet, Lucretius scholar).
- **The same physical laws on earth and in the heavens** [`universal_physical_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_physical_laws.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Aristotelian teaching distinguishes the sublunary elements from the heavens. Cusanus questioned the division. Comparing celestial and terrestrial motions would challenge it.
- **Mechanical philosophy (explain by matter and motion, not hidden purposes)** [`mechanical_philosophy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_philosophy.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Engineers think this way about machines; philosophers explain by forms, purposes and occult virtues. Sounds Epicurean.
- **Idea of progress (knowledge accumulates, the future can be better)** [`idea_of_progress`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/idea_of_progress.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. The ideal is recovering antiquity. Still, Florentines are proud of the dome, printing, compass and guns; Alberti thought the moderns equal the ancients.
- **Invention as a method (organised research and development)** [`systematic_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/systematic_invention.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Engineers build scale models and keep notebooks (Brunelleschi, Taccola, Francesco di Giorgio, Leonardo) but work alone, in secret, for one patron. Local: Opera del Duomo (models); Francesco di Giorgio Martini (Siena).
- **Golden rule and universal ethics** [`golden_rule_universal_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/golden_rule_universal_ethics.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Matthew 7:12 supplies a familiar Christian formulation. Slavery, confessional divisions and unequal civic standing complicate its application.
- **Human equality and dignity** [`human_equality_dignity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/human_equality_dignity.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Souls are equal before God, ranks on earth are natural. Pico's Oration (1486) praises human dignity. Florentine households keep slaves. Local: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola.
- **Natural (human) rights** [`natural_rights`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_rights.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Canon lawyers distinguish natural law from enacted statutes. Local entitlements also depend on status, citizenship and guild membership.
- **Social contract (government by consent)** [`social_contract`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_contract.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Republican tradition (Bruni) and Marsilius of Padua place authority in the citizens. Saying so too loudly under the Medici is risky; welcome after 1494. Local: Bartolomeo Scala (chancellor); anti-Medici families.
- **Freedom of thought, speech and the press** [`freedom_of_speech_thought`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/freedom_of_speech_thought.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Humanists enjoy wide licence in Latin among themselves. Pico's theses were condemned in 1487; criticising the regime means exile.
- **Religious toleration and freedom of conscience** [`religious_tolerance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/religious_tolerance.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept low. Jews are tolerated as licensed moneylenders under Medici protection; friars preach against them. Cusanus and Pico imagine concord of faiths. Heresy is a crime.
- **Secular state (separation of religious and civil authority)** [`secular_state`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secular_state.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Dante's Monarchia and Marsilius argue it. Florence has fought popes (interdict 1478) but no one separates faith from law.
- **Utilitarianism (judge rules by their consequences for everyone)** [`utilitarianism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/utilitarianism.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. The 'common good' (bene comune) is standard civic rhetoric, but it means the city's honour and peace, not a sum of everyone's welfare.
- **Abolition of judicial torture; proportionate, certain punishment** [`abolition_of_torture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_torture.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Judicial torture (the strappado, 'la corda') is ordinary legal procedure under Roman law; confession is the queen of proofs. Local: Bargello; Otto di Guardia.
- **Positive-sum cooperation (trade is not zero-sum)** [`positive_sum_cooperation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/positive_sum_cooperation.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Merchants live by it; Archbishop Antoninus (d. 1459) defended fair trade. Policy between cities and guilds is zero-sum: bans, monopolies, tariffs.
- **Game theory (prisoner's dilemma, credible commitment)** [`game_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/game_theory.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Italian diplomats and condottieri reason this way by instinct; no vocabulary for it.
- **Commons problem and how communities solve it** [`tragedy_of_the_commons`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tragedy_of_the_commons.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Village statutes regulate pasture, woods and water. Tuscan forest management and the Sienese pasture office provide precedents for governing shared resources. Local: Camaldoli and Vallombrosa forests; Sienese Dogana dei Paschi (Maremma pastures).
